config.title: useToggle

intro.title: useToggle
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a custom React hook called `useToggle` that manages a boolean state value and provides a function to toggle it. You will learn how to encapsulate stateful logic into a reusable hook, a core concept in React for sharing functionality across components. The main technologies involved are React's built-in `useState` hook and JavaScript functions. By the end, you'll understand how to create and use custom hooks to make your components cleaner and more maintainable.
intro.usecase: The useToggle pattern appears constantly in modern web applications where users need to switch between binary states. For example, in e-commerce sites, you'll see toggles for showing/hiding product filters, expanding/collapsing product descriptions, or enabling/disabling notifications. In dashboard applications, developers use toggles to control sidebar visibility, switch between light/dark themes, or activate/deactivate data auto-refresh. This pattern simplifies managing boolean state changes across components, making your code cleaner and more maintainable.

objectives: Implement a custom useToggle hook from scratch
Apply the useToggle hook to manage boolean state in functional components
Construct a toggle handler that flips the boolean value
Configure the useToggle hook to accept an initial state parameter
Update component UI based on the toggle state value
Bind the toggle handler to user interface elements like buttons
Integrate multiple useToggle instances within a single component

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in the necessary modules for building React components and managing state.
steps.analogousExample:

import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary React APIs are imported and ready to use in your component.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing both React and useState from the 'react' package.
steps.feedbackWrong: import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package using the import statement.

steps.title: Create the useToggle custom hook
steps.instruction: Create a function named useToggle that takes an initial value as a parameter.
steps.hint: Define a function that accepts one parameter, which will be the initial state for the toggle.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the useToggle function here
steps.expectedOutcome: A useToggle function is defined with one parameter for the initial value.
successCriteria: A function named useToggle exists and accepts one parameter.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've defined a function named useToggle that takes one parameter.
steps.feedbackWrong: The useToggle function isn't defined correctly. It should be a function that accepts one parameter.

steps.title: Initialize state inside useToggle
steps.instruction: Inside the useToggle function, call useState with the initialValue parameter and destructure the returned state and setter into variables named 'state' and 'setState'.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported earlier. The initial state should be the value passed to the hook as a parameter.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useToggle function will have a state variable and setter ready to manage the toggle value.
successCriteria: useState is called with initialValue, and the returned array is destructured into 'state' and 'setState' variables.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're calling useState with the initialValue parameter and destructuring the result into two variables.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's focus on initializing state. Inside useToggle, you need to call useState(initialValue) and destructure the result.

steps.title: Define the toggle function
steps.instruction: Inside the useToggle function, define a function named toggle that calls the state setter with the opposite of the current state value.
steps.hint: You can create a function that uses the setState function from useState to update the state to !currentValue.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useToggle hook will have a toggle function that can be called to switch the boolean value.
successCriteria: A toggle function is defined inside useToggle that calls setValue with !value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your toggle function calls setValue with the opposite of the current value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The toggle function isn't defined correctly. It should call setValue(!value) to toggle the boolean state.

steps.title: Return values from useToggle
steps.instruction: Return an array containing the current state value and the toggle function from the useToggle hook.
steps.hint: At the end of your useToggle function, use the return statement to provide both the state value and the toggle function in an array.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useToggle hook now returns an array with the current boolean state and a function to toggle it, making them available to any component that calls the hook.
successCriteria: The useToggle function returns an array containing the state value and the toggle function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're returning both the state value and the toggle function in an array format.
steps.feedbackWrong: The useToggle hook needs to return an array with the state value and toggle function. Check that your return statement includes both values.

steps.instruction: Define a functional component named App that returns JSX.
steps.hint: Create a function called App that returns a JSX element, like a div.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is defined and ready to use the useToggle hook.

steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Use the useToggle hook in App

steps.hint: Call useToggle(false) and destructure the array into something like [value, toggle].

const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will have access to the toggle state and function from the custom hook.

steps.title: Add a button to toggle the state
steps.instruction: Inside the App component's return statement, add a button element with the text 'Toggle' and an onClick handler that calls the toggle function you destructured from useToggle.
steps.hint: Remember to use JSX syntax for the button and pass the toggle function to onClick without calling it immediately.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component should return a button that, when clicked, will trigger the toggle function from useToggle.
successCriteria: A button element with text 'Toggle' and an onClick handler that calls the toggle function is added to the App component's return statement.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the button has the correct text and the onClick handler is properly set to the toggle function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button or onClick handler is missing or incorrect. Check that you've added a button with the text 'Toggle' and an onClick handler that calls the toggle function.

steps.title: Export the App component
